passage: Coach's note, written by Imran. Harsha has been at the practice centre for four months. In the last two weeks Harsha's mock scores fell sharply, and the answer sheets showed careless mistakes. I asked casually about sleep. Harsha admitted to four hours a night for two weeks. We looked at the score sheets together and noticed that every low score followed a stretch of late nights. Harsha decided the plan itself was the problem. The new plan: lights out at the same time, a twenty-minute walk in the evening, and one evening a week with no books. I only suggested writing the pattern on paper. Two weeks later, accuracy on the mock had risen and Harsha looked more settled.

qa.q: How many hours a night did Harsha sleep for two weeks?
qa.a: Harsha slept four hours a night for two weeks.

qa.q: What was Harsha likely feeling when the scores dropped?
qa.a: Harsha was probably worried and worn down, since the scores fell sharply and the late nights had been eating into rest.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Harsha add for the days when scores dip anyway, and why?
qa.a: Harsha could talk to a counsellor or a trusted person about the pressure, because a schedule helps the body but stress may need a person to talk to.

qa.q: How does Imran see Harsha's progress?
qa.a: Imran sees Harsha finding the link between late nights and low scores without being told, so Imran only suggests writing the pattern down and notices calmer accuracy later.

grounding: Shows an aspirant noticing that scores fall after sleepless stretches and building rest, movement and a free evening into the plan.

passage:
Sunday night
Looked at my mock scores for the last two months side by side. There's a pattern and I hate it: every time I've had a week of 2 am nights, the next Sunday's accuracy drops. 71%, 72%, then 64% after the late week. 70%, then 61% after the other late week.
Urmila said it last month and I didn't listen: "You're studying tired, not studying more."
So, new rules from tomorrow:
Lights off at 11. Fixed. Even if a chapter is half done.
A 20-minute walk to the park and back at 6 pm, no phone.
Friday evening off. Completely. A film with Urmila, or sleep.
Two Sundays later, adding this:
The first week felt like wasting time. The second week's mock: 74%. My best yet. I'm annoyed that Urmila was right, and relieved.
Ayesha

qa.q: What time are lights off under the new rules?
How does Ayesha feel about the 74% result?
qa.a: Ayesha feels relieved and a little annoyed that Urmila was right about studying tired.

qa.q: What else could Ayesha watch for in the coming weeks?
qa.a: Ayesha could keep noting sleep and scores side by side, so any new dip is spotted early.

qa.q: How might Urmila see Ayesha's change?
qa.a: Urmila, whose warning was ignored at first, would likely be glad to see it heeded and to share Friday evenings.

grounding: Shows an aspirant noticing that scores dip after sleepless weeks, adding fixed sleep, an evening walk and a free evening, and seeing accuracy improve.
